The smallest such integer is $n = 8$.

Let $P(n) = 1!\,2!\cdots(n-1)!$. Checking each $n$ directly:

| $n$ | $P(n)$ | $(n!)^2$ | $P(n) > (n!)^2$? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1 | No |
| 2 | 1 | 4 | No |
| 3 | 2 | 36 | No |
| 4 | 12 | 576 | No |
| 5 | 288 | 14400 | No |
| 6 | 34560 | 518400 | No |
| 7 | 24883200 | 25401600 | No |
| 8 | 125411328000 | 1625702400 | Yes |

For $n = 7$: $P(7) = 34560 \cdot 720 = 24883200$, while $(7!)^2 = 5040^2 = 25401600$, so the inequality fails narrowly.

For $n = 8$: $P(8) = 24883200 \cdot 5040 = 125411328000$, while $(8!)^2 = 40320^2 = 1625702400$, so the inequality holds.

Thus $n = 8$ is the smallest positive integer satisfying the inequality.

ANSWER: 8
